note: A CHURCH COULD NOT REMOVE ONE ROW FROM A CONTACT'S TIMELINE. A note typed on the wrong contact, a call logged twice, a meeting that did not happen - all permanent. THE HARD PART WAS NEVER THE DELETE BUTTON, IT WAS THE DONATION. A donation activity carries `invoiceId` and `invoiceAmountCents`, and THE INVOICE IS THE MONEY: the dashboard giving figure sums `tenants/{t}/invoices`, AdminAccounting reads it, `/api/giving-statements/generate` aggregates it per donor per year and `/api/donation-history` is how a MEMBER sees their own giving, while `contactActivities` is read as money by nothing at all - THE-350 made `amount` null on these rows precisely so nothing sums a gift twice. So a delete that removed only the row would leave the money behind in every one of the three reasons a church deletes one (logged on the wrong contact, typed at the wrong amount, never happened), with the church watching the row vanish and reasonably concluding the figure had moved. THE FOUNDER'S DECISION SETTLED IT - 'make sure that if i delete the activity, it is deleted from the dashboard analytics donation as well' - and because the dashboard reads INVOICES, that means the INVOICE IS DELETED WITH THE ACTIVITY. Not anonymised: anonymising is `member-erasure.ts`'s job under a different lawful basis and deliberately KEEPS the money while removing the person, which is the opposite of a church correcting its own record, and an anonymised receipt still counts on the dashboard - the one thing the founder asked for the removal of. IT IS A SECOND ROUTE AND NOT A BRANCH IN THE FIRST, which is this ticket's answer to its own STOP condition 4 rather than a dodge. `contact-activities/route.ts` already exports a DELETE that removes EVERY activity of one contact for THE-362's cascade, and that route's docblock spends a section on what it does NOT touch: `tenants/{t}/invoices` IS NEVER READ OR WRITTEN HERE. Deleting a PERSON keeps their receipts; deliberately deleting ONE GIFT does not. Two different acts with two opposite answers, and a shared handler would have had to choose between them from the shape of a query string - so the new handler lives at `contact-activities/[activityId]/route.ts`, the collection route is BYTE-IDENTICAL to what THE-362 left, and a digest guard pins it so the decision cannot leak into the cascade later either. `manageCRM` IS THE RIGHT BAR AND IT IS NOT RAISED, WHICH IS THE ANSWER TO STOP CONDITION 2. firestore.rules gates invoices on `manageAccounting` and the CRM admin who records a gift holds `manageCRM`, which is why THE-350's write runs on the Admin SDK behind a `manageCRM` route rather than from the client; this is the same wall from the other side and the answer is the same shape, so NO RULE CHANGED, no client gained access, and the rule is asserted as it stands. Requiring `manageAccounting` would put the correction out of reach of exactly the person who made the mistake - the founder's original bug wearing a permission error, the trade THE-350 already refused once. WHAT MAKES THAT SAFE IS NOT THE PERMISSION, IT IS THE SOURCE CHECK: the invoice is READ before anything is deleted and the operation is REFUSED unless it carries `source: 'crm_manual'`, a gift a manageCRM admin typed into this very screen, so the delete bar and the AUTHORSHIP bar are the same bar and this route can only undo what a CRM admin created through the CRM. A processed receipt (no `source` at all - which every historical receipt is, and which `isManuallyRecordedDonation` reads as processed) is refused; so is anything outside the declared set, and the set itself is PINNED so a third manual source added tomorrow turns the suite red rather than silently inheriting this ticket's answer. AN EVENT TICKET IS REFUSED, AND NOT FOR THE REASON THE TICKET EXPECTED - STOP condition 5 was checked and does not fire. `paymentStateOf` reads the `paymentInvoiceId` STRING on the registration and NEVER FETCHES THE INVOICE, and the check-in path reads registration status alone, so deleting the receipt could not revoke a ticket anybody holds. It is refused for the opposite reason: the ticket survives AND SO DOES THE CONFIRMED STATE, with no way back - `paymentInvoiceId` is also THE-351's permanent idempotence guard, so a second Confirm returns the dead id without writing, and the queue key was deleted so the row has left the inbox. The church would hold a ticket it says is paid for, no receipt on its books, and a Confirm button that can never write the gift again. That is a one-way trap, not the correction the founder asked for, so the route refuses and says so on screen; correcting an event payment belongs to the event, where the registration and the receipt can move together. IT IS ATOMIC, BECAUSE HERE IT CAN BE. The collection route argues RESUMABLE over ATOMIC and is right to - a batch cannot span an unbounded timeline - but this is exactly TWO documents, so a transaction spans them and either both go or neither does. That matters because one ordering is UNRECOVERABLE: activity-first would mean a failure that removes the row and leaves the gift on the books with no pointer left to find it by, and no screen left to retry from. Asserted by making the COMMIT fail, which is the only thing that tells a transaction from two sequential deletes. `totalDonated` IS DECREMENTED ON THE CLIENT AND THAT IS THE ONLY SAFE PLACE: it is a client-maintained running total that `addActivity` bumps with a read-modify-write of a value the component already holds, and THE-359 declined to bump it from a server route precisely because a server write would race that one, so the subtraction is the same read-modify-write in the same component, symmetric with the bump and racing nothing. Leaving it would overstate the person's giving permanently and, because `resolvePipelineStage` is a function of it, park them in a stage their giving no longer supports. `lastDonationAt` is deliberately not rewound. THE NON-DONATION CASE IS A HARD DELETE WITH A CONFIRMATION, one behaviour and not two: a timeline full of tombstones is worse than a lost note, and one confirmation for every type means one code path rather than a length heuristic deciding when a church gets a warning. Anyone with `manageCRM` may delete, not only the author - a church tidying its own records should not be blocked by who typed the row. NO GIFT IS EVER DELETED SILENTLY, and the structural half of that is that a gift whose amount cannot be read on screen offers NO DELETE BUTTON AT ALL. A DOWNLOADED RECEIPT IS NOT ORPHANED BY THIS AND THE COPY SAYS NOTHING ABOUT IT, which was checked rather than assumed: `recordManualDonation` writes `pdfUrl: null`, nothing generates a PDF for a manual gift, and the download route refuses an empty path before signing anything - so no member can be holding a downloaded receipt for a gift this route can reach, and a sentence about it would warn about something that cannot happen. NO npm DEPENDENCY, NO THEME TOKEN AND NO NEW PRIMITIVE was installed, and no primitive was composed into AdminCRM: the row action uses the `dropdown-menu` already on disk, the confirmation is the file's existing hand-rolled dialog shape and the refusal is the `alert` primitive THE-362 already put there. `firestore.rules`, `firestore.indexes.json`, `functions/` and `src/app/layout.tsx` are byte-identical and asserted so - no composite index is needed because both routes run one single-field query or a get by document id and neither builds a query an index could serve. NINETEEN MUTATIONS WERE PLANTED AND EVERY ONE WAS CAUGHT, three of them only after the guard that should have caught it was found blind: a Stripe receipt deleting through the processed-gift branch (the fixture never reached it), a failed delete refetching the timeline (asserted on the DOM, which a stubbed hook makes vacuous - it now asserts the INVALIDATION, which is the thing that actually removes a row), and a non-atomic rewrite (the first mutation only reordered two buffered deletes, which is not a defect).

entries.why: THE-369 adds a ROW ACTION and a CONFIRMATION to this file, and one write. A church could not remove a single activity from a contact's timeline - a note typed on the wrong contact, a call logged twice, a meeting that did not happen were all permanent - so each timeline row gains a dropdown-menu carrying one Delete item, and pressing it opens a dialog that must be read before anything is destroyed. THE ROW ACTION IS THE INSTALLED PRIMITIVE, not a bare bin icon: a destructive control sitting open on every row is one mis-tap from a deleted gift, and `dropdown-menu` is what this repo installs for a row action - the same three-dot trigger, the same min-h-11/sm:min-h-0 pair and the same z-[110] as AdminDocs, whose note on that z-index applies here unchanged. THE CONFIRMATION NAMES THE AMOUNT AND WHAT CHANGES, because 'this cannot be undone' is not enough where a receipt is being destroyed - #506 established that standard on the contact dialog one layer up, and here the deletion reaches five places at once, so the copy names the figure through `formatCents` (never the dollar formatter - reading cents with it is AdminAccounting's own $10,550,000 bug, and doing it above a Delete button would be that bug with a church's approval underneath it), says the receipt leaves the books rather than only the timeline, and names the dashboard giving figure, the accounting totals, the member's own giving history, their giving statement and the receipt-number gap. A GIFT WHOSE AMOUNT CANNOT BE READ GETS NO DELETE BUTTON AT ALL, on the `alert` primitive this repo installs for a refusal: a confirmation that cannot state what it is about must not carry one, which is the structural half of 'no receipt is ever deleted silently' rather than a warning that could be ignored, and the same guard is repeated in the handler because a refusal living only in markup is one re-render away from being bypassed. ONE `setDoc` IS ADDED AND IT IS THE `totalDonated` DECREMENT: the total is client-maintained and `addActivity` bumps it with a read-modify-write of a value this component already holds, so the subtraction is the same read-modify-write in the same component - THE-359 declined to bump it from a server route precisely because a server write would race this one, and doing the decrement anywhere else would reintroduce that race. `lastDonationAt` is deliberately NOT rewound: answering 'when did they last give' after a deletion needs the whole timeline, and a guessed date would be a new false fact where a stale one is only a display fact. A FAILED DELETE SURFACES VISIBLY AND REMOVES NOTHING - the dialog stays open on the row it failed on with the reason inside it, the row is still on the timeline underneath because nothing is removed optimistically, and the invalidation that would refetch the timeline sits INSIDE the `try` after the throw, which is exactly the line #506 moved one layer up. THE DELETE HANDLER LIVES BELOW `sendEmail` RATHER THAN BESIDE `addActivity`, WHICH IS ITS MIRROR, AND THAT PLACEMENT IS A GUARD RATHER THAN TASTE: THE-350 asserts the CRM's ledger-first ordering and its kept-input failure path by SLICING this file from `const addActivity = async` to `const sendEmail = async` and reading the last catch in the slice, so a second async function inside that span moves what that guard reads onto code it was never written about - measured, not guessed, because the first arrangement of this ticket went red reporting `addActivity` as having lost its error banner when `addActivity` had not changed by one byte. This ticket moved its own code rather than relaxing that guard. NOTHING THE PREVIOUS TICKETS OWN WAS DISTURBED: THE-368's single GivingDocsLink is still the only one and still inside the `actForm.type === 'donation'` branch, and the delete dialog deliberately renders no link of its own because a fourth page would have to be inlined and the page is a CLOSED UNION whose label is derived from it; THE-350's `addActivity` is byte-identical including `amount: null`, `invoiceId`, `invoiceAmountCents`, the ledger-first ordering and both notices; THE-362's two delete refusals, its single dialog definition and its activities-first/contact-last cascade are untouched, and the cascade still calls the collection route exactly once; #482's payment-links disclaimer keeps its text and its keepMounted fold and the Contacts/Roles switcher is still ONE subTabBar rendered on both sub-views. NO COLOUR IS HARDCODED - the file's nine hexes are unmoved and this ticket adds no tenth; the only new '#' sequences in the whole diff are the ticket references #500 and #506 inside docblocks, which every content grep here reads through #496's parser-backed stripper precisely so a ticket number is never read as a CSS shorthand. Every control this ticket adds carries 44px below sm and Rule 4's imported CONTROL_DENSITY.control above it, measured in a real Chromium with transitions suppressed, and the icon-only row trigger is measured on WIDTH as well as height because THE-308 found a control that cleared the floor on height at 35.6px wide. No new token, component or dependency.

THE-369 raises ONE NUMBER in this file and adds the paragraph that says why: RULES_PINNERS_NOW goes 77 to 78, because this ticket's guard suite is a new pinner that reaches the accepted rules-digest set through the shared module. THE REASON IS THE STRONGEST ON THAT LIST. This ticket lets a church DELETE a `tenants/{t}/invoices` receipt, and that collection's rule is the one thing standing between a CRM admin and the money ledger - `allow write: if hasPermission('manageAccounting', tenantId)`. A reviewer of a ticket that deletes receipts is entitled to know the rule did not move an inch to permit it. It did not, and it could not usefully: the delete runs on the Admin SDK behind a route that imposes `requireTenantPermission(request, tenantId, 'manageCRM')` itself, which is exactly the posture THE-350 established for the invoice WRITE when it hit the same wall from the other side, and no client gains any access at all. THE COUNT IS RAISED, NEVER LOOSENED - the floor exists to catch a suite that quietly STOPS pinning, and that still fails; no pinner was retired, no accepted value was widened and no digest was replaced. THE-369 RECORDS NO firestore.rules DIGEST OF ITS OWN in this directory: #464 established that the ownership register is PER TICKET and a rules digest written into it turned THE-325 red for two tickets running, so the suite reaches the value through `rulesDigestFailure()` and spells no hash anywhere. Nothing else in this file moved: every ownership assertion, the validate refusals, the population pins and the unrecorded-digest checks are byte-identical.
